description: Zenith Horizon is building an interactive browser-based space mission simulation game using open NASA data for the 2026 Space Apps Challenge.
summary: ASTRION is an interactive 3D space mission design game that teaches real aerospace engineering trade-offs. Players configure rockets, orbits, power, comms, and science payloads under strict mass and budget limits, then fly their custom spacecraft from Earth launch through asteroid navigation, planetary EVA exploration, and Earth return.
details:
ASTRION — Interactive 3D Space Exploration Game

Developed by: Team Zenith Horizon

Project Overview

ASTRION is an interactive 3D space exploration game designed to bring the excitement of space travel, planetary exploration, and scientific discovery into an immersive digital experience. It allows players to experience a space mission, from preparing a spacecraft and launching from Earth to travelling through space, approaching the Moon, landing on its surface, and exploring the lunar environment.

Our goal is to make space exploration more engaging and accessible by combining interactive gameplay, realistic 3D environments, spacecraft controls, and space-related information in one experience.

How Does It Work?

ASTRION takes players through different stages of a space exploration mission.

Players begin by preparing and configuring their spacecraft before starting their journey. They can launch from Earth, navigate through space, and experience flight using cockpit and external camera views. The game also features a Moon exploration experience where players can approach and land on the lunar surface.

After landing, players can explore the environment, collect samples, and capture photographs. The game also includes asteroid encounters and integrates NASA's Near Earth Object Web Service (NeoWs) to retrieve asteroid-related information. When live data is unavailable, clearly identified sample data is used as a fallback.

The experience combines interactive controls, 3D environments, camera systems, and mission-based gameplay to create an engaging exploration journey.

Benefits and Intended Impact

ASTRION aims to encourage curiosity about astronomy, space science, planetary environments, and space exploration technologies.

Its main benefits include:

  • Educational Engagement: Encourages users to explore space-related concepts through interactive experiences.
  • Scientific Curiosity: Introduces players to asteroids, planetary environments, lunar exploration, and space missions.
  • Interactive Learning: Makes exploration more engaging than simply reading about space.
  • Creativity and Problem-Solving: Encourages players to interact with spacecraft systems and complete exploration objectives.
  • Accessibility: Provides a digital space exploration experience without requiring physical space equipment or specialized hardware.

Our intended impact is to inspire interest in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM), particularly among students and young people.

Technologies and Tools Used

ASTRION was developed using modern web development technologies and 3D graphics tools.

Programming Languages:

  • TypeScript
  • JavaScript
  • HTML
  • CSS

Frameworks and Libraries:

  • React — User interface development.
  • Vite — Development environment and build tooling.
  • Three.js — 3D graphics and rendering.
  • React Three Fiber — Integration of Three.js with React.
  • React Three Drei — Supporting 3D components and utilities.
  • Zustand — Application state management.
  • Express.js — Server-side functionality.
  • WebSockets — Real-time communication.

External Data Integration:

  • NASA Near Earth Object Web Service (NeoWs) API for asteroid-related information.

Development Environment:

  • Visual Studio Code
  • Node.js and npm
  • Git and GitHub

The project was developed and tested on a Windows-based computer.

Creativity and Innovation

The creative aspect of ASTRION is its combination of space exploration, interactive spacecraft experiences, and 3D planetary environments within a web-based game.

Instead of presenting space as a collection of static images or information screens, ASTRION allows players to participate in an exploration journey. The combination of spacecraft configuration, launch sequences, cockpit and external camera perspectives, lunar landing, surface exploration, sample collection, and asteroid encounters creates a connected gameplay experience.

The use of NASA's publicly available asteroid data also adds a connection between the game and real-world space science.

Factors Considered During Development

Our team considered several important factors while developing ASTRION:

  1. User Experience: We aimed for intuitive navigation and interactive controls.
  2. Visual Quality: We focused on immersive 3D environments and a professional space-themed interface.
  3. Performance: We considered hardware limitations and optimized the experience to run on typical personal computers.
  4. Educational Value: We incorporated space-related concepts and asteroid information to encourage scientific curiosity.
  5. Technical Reliability: We used a structured development approach and tested the project through development and production builds.
  6. Accessibility: We chose web technologies so users can experience the game without installing a traditional desktop game.
  7. Responsible Data and Attribution: We considered the appropriate use and attribution of external data and third-party resources.

Conclusion

ASTRION represents our team's effort to combine creativity, programming, 3D technology, and space science into an interactive experience. Through this project, we aim to make space exploration more engaging, encourage scientific curiosity, and demonstrate how modern web technologies can be used to create immersive educational entertainment.

ASTRION — Explore. Discover. Achieve.

Team Zenith Horizon

ASTRION is an independent project and is not affiliated with or officially endorsed by NASA.

Super Intelligence (SI) Disclosure

ASTRION is an original project conceptualized and planned by Team Zenith Horizon. The team's brainstorming, core concept, project vision, feature selection, gameplay direction, and major development decisions were created by the team.

ChatGPT (OpenAI), a large language model, was used as a coding assistant for selected code generation, debugging, troubleshooting, and technical guidance. It also assisted with drafting and editing project documentation, including the project description.

AI image-generation tools were used to create visual assets, including the ASTRION logo and YouTube thumbnail.

Team Zenith Horizon directed the development process, made the final design and implementation decisions, and reviewed and tested the project. The team remains responsible for the final work.

AI-generated visual assets were also created for the Earth launch ground and Mars surface environments using an AI agent.

NASA asteroid information is retrieved through NASA's Near Earth Object Web Service (NeoWs) API. This data is retrieved from NASA and is not AI-generated.
